items.title: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.topic: Enhancement of Large Language Models Driving Knowledge for Practical Autonomous Driving Decision Making
items.summary: The IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology published a study on enhancing large language models (LLMs) for practical autonomous driving decision-making. The paper introduces a question-guided multimodal graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (QGM-GRAG) approach to improve the theoretical driving knowledge of LLMs, addressing the need for safety-critical autonomous driving tasks. The method leverages structured textual rules and visual traffic signs to enhance LLMs' hazard perception and decision-making capabilities.

items.title: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.topic: A Collaborative Multi-Modality Interaction for VLA-based End-to-End Autonomous Driving
items.summary: A study published in arXiv proposes a robust Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model for end-to-end autonomous driving that integrates multi-modality interaction with multi-trajectory planning and optimization. The model aims to improve reliable and interpretable decision-making in long-tail driving scenarios by combining perception, reasoning, and decision-making within a unified multimodal framework.

items.title: PlannerForge: LLM Agents for Scenario-Based Testing of Motion Planners in Autonomous Driving
items.topic: PlannerForge: LLM Agents for Scenario-Based Testing of Motion Planners in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: PlannerForge, an LLM-agent framework for scenario-based testing of Autonomous Driving Systems (ADSs), was introduced in arXiv. The framework extends all stages of scenario-based testing, from generation to assessment, and adds two new stages: ADS Enhancement and ADS Assessment. By integrating LLMs across the entire pipeline, PlannerForge aims to improve the systematic validation and safety of ADSs.
